title: Are Yields Rising Too Fast For Banks?

Are Yields Rising Too Fast For Banks?

Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 9 Oct 2026

US bank stocks have lagged the broader equity market since the start of September, with the S&P 500 bank index down -7.5% against a 1% gain for the S&P 500. Curiously, this has happened during an inflationary boom, which should favor banks. While higher yields typically benefit lenders by allowing them to charge more on loans and earn higher returns on their securities holdings, a rapid rise in yields, as in 2021-22, can break things and hurt the sector. Equity investors may be worried about this risk. However, with US commercial banks set to start reporting earnings next week, there are reasons to think these concerns will prove short-lived.According to the Citi Economic Surprise index, US growth data delivered increasingly positive surprises in September. Meanwhile, energy prices continued to rise amid attacks on pipelines and refineries in the Persian Gulf and Russia. As a result, US bond yields rose sharply across the curve. Stronger lending prospects and higher borrowing rates should have benefited US banks. Yet bank stocks underperformed.
